# Complete Hello quoting engine through explicit C services

This component replaces the complete retained quoting loop used by the native
Hello quoting callers. It follows the practical workflow: manually define the
boundary, author ordinary C, compare against the actual PE32 routine, edit and
replay discrepancies, then execute the selected C through real consumers.
No new solver model, proof rule or comparison format is involved.

The accepted public run is
`build/hello-quote-engine-2026-09-22/workflow-v1/`: 59 commands and 50 comparisons
pass, including seven-component experimental build/test. The retained
`checkpoint-audit.json` revalidates receipts and current code bindings. The actual
terminal Hello regression, connected jq regression, 13 targeted Nix tests and six
repository/SDK gates also pass. This is an experimental checkpoint; complete
whole-program qualification remains open.

The subsequent [conversion-family checkpoint](../hello-multibyte/README.md)
prepares this engine with `--multibyte-package /path/to/multibyte-conversion`.
Its existing dependency graph selects authored conversion/reset operations in
both local and native-consumer comparisons. A fourth, explicitly controlled UTF-8
service context raises the engine matrix to 220 cases and 24,640 transformations
per side; it is separate from the native locales described below. Public editing,
three-level discrepancy replay and an eight-unit experimental run pass. Omitting
that option retains the independent engine comparison with original services.

The algorithm reference is GNU Hello 2.12.3 `lib/quotearg.c`, written by Paul
Eggert. `COPYING.hello` retains its GPL license. This is source-assisted authoring;
the pinned original executable is the independent comparison oracle. It is not
evidence that arbitrary source-unavailable programs are equally easy to lift.

## Boundary and ownership

The original executable has SHA-256
`71b228f2babc9d3b4095ecf355db676c8ed8b45a7c8a7d350f47e962b4bf554c`.
The manually selected engine owns `[36ea,4eb3)` and the invalid-style cold region
`[14640,14645)`, in RVA notation. The retained transfer plan contains 531 transfers
in these ranges, including 13 calls. This inventory is not checked control-flow
coverage or qualification. The public operation is the original buffer quoting
operation; private C helpers do not create synthetic production interfaces.

| Boundary value | Executable interpretation |
|---|---|
| Output and capacity | Borrowed writable bytes; writes stop at capacity while the returned required length continues to advance |
| Argument and size | Borrowed current bytes, with either an explicit length or the target's `UINT32_MAX` NUL-terminated sentinel |
| Style and flags | All eleven styles, NUL elision, optional outer quotes and trigraph splitting |
| Eight-word mask | Current mutable words; byte writes through an overlapping output remain visible to later mask reads |
| Custom delimiters | Borrowed NUL-terminated byte strings; locale styles obtain actual native locale quotes |
| Conversion object | A private four-byte target state plus a separate character result, transported through explicit services |

`quote-buffer.c` uses ordinary C loops, private helpers and typed service calls.
The generated interface has eight synchronous services: maximum character width,
locale quotes, byte classification, conversion reset/decode/initial-state, wide
character classification and invalid-style termination. `bridge.c` supplies the
reviewed native implementations. The source contains no PE addresses, Win32 calls,
machine register state or native quoting-algorithm fallback.

The byte objects are call-scoped proxies for live pointers. They do not copy input
spans or reconstruct memory from numeric identities. The mask is also live, rather
than snapshotted at entry. The native bridge alone carries the pinned calling
conventions, addresses and four-byte conversion-state relation. It does not claim
that a host `mbstate_t` has that layout. A null original mask becomes a private
all-zero mask; private recursive calls can also omit the mask.

Valid readable/writable extents and required NUL termination are premises. Borrowed
objects must remain live throughout each synchronous call. Declarations and these
adapters are executable transport, not checked memory/effect summaries. Arbitrary
callbacks, concurrency, service side effects and unbounded size arithmetic are
not established by the finite examples.

## Cases and observations

The local matrix has 165 cases: eleven styles, five flag combinations and three
requested CRT locales. Each case makes 112 transformations from 28 inputs and
four storage modes. It covers empty/ASCII/control bytes, embedded NULs, shell and
custom delimiter punctuation, trigraphs, all byte values, generated bytes,
UTF-8-encoded byte strings, Shift-JIS bytes and invalid/incomplete sequences.
Capacities include zero and truncation; explicit-size modes overlap output with
the input and with mask bytes. All 18,480 transformations per side match in the
retained `matrix-v3` run.

Observations include required length, errno, every initialized output/argument
byte, live mask words and poison frames around the output and mask. The reported
maximum character widths are 1 for `C`, 1 for `.65001` and 2 for
`Japanese_Japan.932` in the retained runtime. The `.65001` name therefore does
**not** establish UTF-8 multibyte execution; the Japanese locale exercises the
multibyte path. The original width helper reads the actual CRT width cell.
No locale behavior is synthesized to obtain a desired result.

The original image uses the existing test-only loader-header adaptation, with
original section bytes preserved. Driver CRT initialization replaces original
startup/TLS execution. Invalid styles, original startup, arbitrary locale
environments and all possible access traces remain outside the returning-case
matrix. The invalid-style C branch calls the real abort service, but that branch
is not exercised by this matrix.

## Reproduce the public workflow

Use `nix develop .#lifting` and the
[fresh connected recipe](../hello-handoff/README.md) for setup from original inputs.
This component's preparation accepts the original and output alone to discover
the shell's pinned tools. Supplying a retained PE32 comparison package explicitly,
as below, still reuses only its tools and compiler runtime DLLs. The pinned Hello
executable is a separate input. Preparation does not rebuild a pilot.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=.:src python tests/fixtures/hello-quote-engine/prepare.py \
  /path/to/retained-pe32-comparison/inputs /path/to/original/hello.exe \
  build/hello-quote-engine-packages
```

The [native quoting recipe](../hello-native-quoting/README.md) accepts the prepared
package alongside the existing cleanup, realloc and checked-allocation packages:

```sh
env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH -u LD_PRELOAD -u GCC_EXEC_PREFIX -u COMPILER_PATH \
  PYTHONPATH=.:src spaghetti-headless-wayland \
  python tests/fixtures/hello-native-quoting/walkthrough.py \
  build/hello-components /path/to/retained-pe32-comparison/inputs \
  /path/to/original/hello.exe build/hello-engine-workflow --component-packages \
  --cleanup-package build/hello-cleanup/quote-cleanup \
  --reallocate-package build/hello-reallocate/allocation-reallocate \
  --checked-allocation-package build/hello-checked/checked-allocation \
  --quote-engine-package build/hello-quote-engine-packages/quote-buffer
```

All Wine applications, boot and server operations run in that headless Wayland
desktop. Preserve the cross-compiler environment, including its target linker
flags. `--quote-engine-package` also works without the other optional packages;
unselected dependencies then remain native.

The recipe uses public `component start/check` and `candidate build/test` commands.
It checks the engine locally and in the connected native network, makes a compatible
source edit and recompiles only the affected translation unit in each check.
The unchanged controlled `quote-slots` caller reuses its local comparison with zero
compiler/link/execution/model/solver work. Its controlled service has no selected
engine body; this is finite local comparison reuse, not a body-independent proof.
The actual native integration correctly reruns when the engine implementation
changes.

A deliberately wrong, defined-C edit substitutes `?` for an embedded NUL that
should be elided. Both the local oracle and an actual quoting caller detect it.
The recipe repairs the draft, replays both retained faulty inputs and reuses the
matching local/integration results. It then builds and runs an explicitly
experimental seven-component selection when all optional packages are supplied.

Native integration overwrites the entire 6,089-byte original main body with traps
except for the entry jump into authored C; it also traps the cold region and
checks the replacement entry counter. The shared fixture hook accepts caller-owned
storage for this larger body. The old bounded inline-storage helper remains
available; its real PE32 test also checks large-body replacement/restoration and
rejects insufficient or overlapping storage.

These results do not authorize strong native selection or complete portable Hello.
Locale/conversion services, lower allocation, other runtime operations and startup
remain native or outside scope. A complete portable selection and second-architecture
execution remain later requirements.
